title: Interdisciplinary secondary prevention and early rehabilitation after geriatric traumatic brain injury
summary:
The study investigates which risk factors can be identified through a multifactorial assessment in patients aged ≥50 years with traumatic brain injury, and to what extent these can be addressed through individualized recommendations. In addition, co-design approaches are used, among other methods, to analyze which barriers and facilitating factors influence the implementation of these recommendations and whether structured counseling can improve adherence. The study is designed as a non-randomized, multicenter, prospective observational study without a control group.
The study population consists of patients to whom the following inclusion and exclusion criteria apply:
Inclusion criteria: age ≥50 years, traumatic brain injury without surgical intervention (Glasgow Coma Scale 13–15), ability to walk 10 meters, residence within ≤50 km of the study center.
Exclusion criteria: concomitant fractures, severe multimorbidity, advanced neurodegenerative diseases, life expectancy <12 months.
The overarching aim is the development of a consensus-based intervention and care model for a future randomized pilot study.

interventions.name:
The non-randomized, multicenter, prospective observational study without a control group comprises three main phases: phenotyping/initial assessment after TBI (T1), provision of individualized recommendations (T2), and follow-up assessment as well as co-design workshops/interviews (T3).
